findings.title: Guidance takes a bodily direction
findings.claim: The guidance-versus-straying contrast reaches the body: the misled are gathered on their faces, without sight, speech, or hearing, so lost guidance is also embodied as lost orientation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries guidance in 17:97:2:1 and 17:97:5:2, misguidance in 17:97:7:1, and a face-first gathering in 17:97:18:1. Fatiha 1:6-7 supplies the straight-path request and its contrast with the astray; 67:22 contrasts face-down movement with upright travel on a straight path; 25:34 joins face-first gathering to Hell and a lost way. The contact makes direction bodily while the focus's physical gathering and impairments remain intact.
findings.reader_payoff: The path requested in Fatiha can now be seen against its embodied contrary: the focus gives misguidance a posture and a route. The gathering, blind sight, failed speech, and deafness form one bodily scene rather than a loose list.
findings.containment: The focus still describes a real gathering and bodily impairments; the path relation adds a contextual resonance without converting those conditions into metaphors or extending them to everyone. 25:73 preserves a contrasting response in which people do not fall deaf and blind when reminded.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run support and focus branch carriers are supplied and trusted. The wider connections provide exact target surfaces but remain nominations, so the integrated path-and-posture reading is qualified.

findings.title: Each lull meets an increase
findings.claim: Every easing of the fire is met by a renewed increase: the repeated condition makes the flame's decline an occasion for further blaze, and a wider punishment scene renews the body's capacity to taste it.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries fire abatement in 17:97:25:1, increase in 17:97:26:1, and blazing fire in 17:97:27:1; kullama at 17:97:24:1 iterates the change. In 4:56, every burned-through skin is replaced so punishment can be tasted again, meeting the focus's renewed blaze through a second bodily mechanism. 78:30 echoes increase as punishment.
findings.reader_payoff: The fire is a process renewed at every lull, while the wider bodily-burning parallel makes continued experience part of that renewal rather than leaving the image as a static place.
findings.containment: This is the focus's punitive cycle, not a rule that fire or increase is always punitive. 5:64 gives a recurring fire that is extinguished, and 48:4 gives an increase in faith; these alternatives bound the local relation without replacing it.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and trusted cross-run support ground the cycle. The wider parallels are exact surface connections but remain contextual nominations, and the qualified heat branch is limited to its supplied physical-fire facet.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Each easing becomes the occasion for renewed punishment rather than release.

findings.title: Refusal returns as bodily closure
findings.claim: The focus's blindness, speechlessness, and deafness can be read as a bodily answer to refused signs: the gathered body carries the closed reception that wider passages place alongside denial and turning away.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies exact carriers for blindness, muteness, and deafness. In 6:39, denial of signs appears with deafness, speechlessness, and darkness before guidance and the straight path are contrasted; in 18:57, people turn away after reminders of signs while hearts are covered, ears weighted, and guidance refused. These wider patterns meet the focus's bodily conditions and make them echo a prior refusal.
findings.reader_payoff: The three impairments remain concrete, while their contact with the refusal passages makes the list legible as more than unrelated bodily conditions: reception and response have become part of the judgment scene.
findings.containment: The focus itself names bodily conditions and does not state a feature-by-feature causal map from sign-denial to each impairment. This is an exploratory contextual reading, not an attributed HFT trace; the literal gathering and impairments remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The HFT summary has no supplied anchor evidence. Exact focus carriers and supplied connection targets independently support a contextual contact, while the recompense relation remains an inference.

findings.title: The failed search is not a power vacuum
findings.claim: The focus denies substitute protectors while keeping divine guardianship active: 42:9 names God as the guardian and raises the dead, so the helpless gathering remains under the authority that can bring the dead to life.
findings.mechanism: The focus's protectors word and besides-Him relation deny alternatives, then its gathering verb names the next act. The exact 42:9 connection places God as guardian beside the raising of the dead; that wider trigger returns through the focus's protectors and gathering, turning the denial of allies into an asymmetrical relation rather than a power vacuum.
findings.reader_payoff: The missing allies describe the gathered group's condition, while divine guardianship and resurrection agency remain present in the wider relation.
findings.containment: This does not promise protection to the people gathered or import the HFT's unsurfaced final-abasement allusion. The 42:9 connection adds divine guardianship and resurrection agency without transferring its target group's status to the focus.

epistemic.reason: The HFT source is unbound, but the focus carrier and exact 42:9 surface support the narrowed asymmetry. The contextual link does not establish that the gathered group receives protection.

branch_activations.activation: The focus denies other supporters, while the wider text names divine guardianship alongside resurrection; the relation returns through the focus's protector word and the gathering act.

branch_activations.boundary: The contextual relation does not transfer 42:9's protective status to the focus's gathered group, and no target-side morphology is inferred.
